args.title: checkout-api: v2.3.1 failed health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api began failing health checks after the latest deploy (v2.3.1) in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an elevated error rate of ~18%. The service was rolled back in all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release with healthy status in production (v2.3.1-rc, seq 2, is staging-only and also unhealthy, so it was not a candidate). Post-rollback verification shows all three regions on v2.3.0 with healthy status and error rate reduced to ~0.2%. Follow-up: root-cause analysis of the v2.3.1 regression before any redeploy, since v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production.

trace.final:
Done.

**What I found:** checkout-api was on v2.3.1 in all three production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), unhealthy, with an ~18% error rate. Release history showed v2.2.9 and v2.3.0 as healthy in production, and v2.3.1-rc unhealthy but staging-only — so v2.3.0 was the correct rollback target.

**Actions taken:**
1. **Rolled back** checkout-api to **v2.3.0** in all production regions — rollout verified.
2. **Confirmed recovery:** all regions on v2.3.0, healthy, error rate down to ~0.2%.
3. **Opened incident INC-0001** (SEV2) for checkout-api, on-call paged, describing the failure, the rollback and target version, and post-rollback verification.

**Note for follow-up:** v2.3.1 has never been healthy in production, so any attempt to redeploy it would require change-manager approval plus a root-cause fix first.
